title: Math — Probability with dice & playing cards
subject: math

questions.prompt: You roll one fair six-sided die once. Its faces show 1 through 6, all equally likely. What is P(rolling a **3**)?
One fair six-sided die. What is P(rolling a **perfect square**, counting only squares among 1–6)?
Roll **two** fair six-sided dice and add the upward faces. What is P(**sum equals 7**)?
Same two dice setup (**36 ordered outcomes**). What is P(**sum equals 11**)?
Same two dice. What is P(**matching numbers — a double** such as rolling 4 twice)?
Same two labelled dice (**36 equally likely ordered rolls**). What is P(the **number on the red die is strictly less than** the blue die)? Count ordered pairs deliberately.
Same two dice. What is P(the **product** of the upward faces equals **12**)?
You shuffle a **standard deck of 52 playing cards**: 4 suits ♠ ♥ ♦ ♣, 13 ranks each (Ace through King), **no jokers**. Randomly reveal **exactly one** card. What is P(**Heart**)?
Same single random card from that **52-card** deck (no reshuffle yet). Treat **Ace** merely as among the four singleton ranks. What is P(drawing **any Ace**)?
Still one random card from **52**. What is P(**Jack, Queen or King**, **any suit**)? There are twelve such faces in a standard deck.
One random card from a **standard 52-card** deck. Hearts and diamonds are **red**; spades and clubs are **black**. What is P(drawing a **red** card)?
One random card from **52**. What is P(**club or diamond**)?
Draw cards **with replacement** each time—you shuffle meticulously after noting every draw so the deck stays freshly **52**. What is P(**first Ace, then Ace again**)?
Now draw **two cards in a row WITHOUT replacement**. What is P(first card **Ace** **and second card King**)?
**Two dice** again (**36 equally likely outcomes**). What is P(sum is **even**)?
